obligations.note: session.py is in SES-1 scope, but the change only alters token length; the idle-timeout logic and policy.PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES are untouched. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy passed in CI on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-25267 was approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-05, before the change opened on 2026-10-07. Its component payments.session covers the only touched file, session.py.
The code_review approval is from sofia.santos, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author mara.costa (none of Costa's addresses appear).
The code_review approval names head commit 20d38cb, so it covers everything being merged.

records/ci/run.json shows success on head commit 20d38cb: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. That includes the registered SES-1 control test, unskipped and passing. I could not rerun it locally because pytest is not installed.

session.py (payments.session) is security_sensitive. The only security_review (kofi.mensah) names 4fd0d0a. The later commit 20d38cb changes TOKEN_BYTES from 24 to 32, a behavioural change, so that review is void and none exists on the final commit.
No protected path (controls/, control tests, ci/) is modified between base and head, so no control_owner approval is needed.
The change is not an emergency (emergency=false, ticket type standard), so no post-implementation review is due.
The change does not rely on any exception. The SES-1 exception for payments.session, EXC-0141, expired on 2026-09-13 and is not invoked; SES-1 is met without it.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers session.py (they cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files), so no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1487 changes only payments/session.py, adding a TOKEN_BYTES constant and raising bearer-token entropy from 24 to 32 bytes. The ticket, the independent code review on the head commit, and CI on the head commit (including the SES-1 control test) are all in order. But session.py is a security-sensitive component, and the only security review was given on the first commit, where TOKEN_BYTES was still 24. The later commit changed behaviour, which voids that review under CHG-5 and CHG-3, so the change cannot be accepted until a security review is recorded on the final commit.
